check: will the 3.65-hour GameTest run be killed by a timeout
risk: A gradle timeout shorter than the run would kill it partway and make the result look like a failure rather than an exhausted budget - the same shape that previously cut off stress runs at five minutes.
finding: runGameTest has no gradle timeout at all, so it can run to completion.

tasksWithTimeout: runServerSmoke, derived from the traversal or stress budget
runServerSmokeProduction, derived from the stress duration
a third task with a flat 5 minutes
deliberateContrast.interpretation: The distinction is deliberate. The smoke tasks drive a server that could hang, so they carry a ceiling; the GameTest task relies on Fabric's own per-case timeout instead.

perCaseProtection.defaultMeaning: the Fabric default of 100 ticks, about 5 seconds
heavyExamples: 1000000 ticks on the combinatorial matrix and component cases
perCaseProtection.consequence: A hung case is failed by Fabric rather than hanging the whole run, so having no gradle ceiling does not create an unbounded risk.

conclusion: Two layers, each doing the job it is suited to: gradle lets the run finish, Fabric stops any single case from hanging.
